key_insight: The paper compares direct and indirect PINN formulations for Dirichlet boundary control of semilinear parabolic PDEs, and shows that the indirect approach admits a structured error decomposition and conditional residual-to-error guarantees.
engineering_relevance: This provides a more reliable PINN framework for PDE-constrained control problems where boundary actuation and optimality conditions must be handled accurately.
method: Direct PINN: separate state/control networks optimize a penalized tracking objective.
Indirect PINN: jointly learns state, adjoint, and control by enforcing the first-order optimality system.
Derives conditional error bounds and a computable residual indicator for the indirect formulation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments on two manufactured test problems, including a cubic reaction-diffusion equation and a linear case with nontrivial boundary control and adjoint.
watch_item: The strongest error guarantees are conditional on regularity, approximability, soft-constraint residual control, and proximity to the reference optimal solution, so practical reliability depends on these assumptions and penalty tuning.
paper_title: Direct and Indirect Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Dirichlet Boundary Control of Semilinear Parabolic Equations: A Conditional Error Analysis
